power_features.trigger_actions: When clock-stop request asserted, M_CAN completes pending transmissions, waits for bus idle, sets CCCR.INIT = 1 internally, then asserts m_can_clkstop_ack + CCCR.CSA = 1.
power_features.abort_path: If bus is heavily disturbed and idle is never reached, CCCR.INIT remains 0; software polls PSR.ACT and may write CCCR.INIT = 1 explicitly to force stop.
wake_up_procedure: 1. External clock controller restarts m_can_hclk + m_can_cclk.
2. CPU deasserts m_can_clkstop_req or clears CCCR.CSR.
5. BSP waits for 11 consecutive recessive bits (Bus_Idle) before joining bus.

low_power_modes_summary.initialization_mode: CCCR.INIT = 1; clocks running; bus output recessive; no Tx/Rx.
low_power_modes_summary.power_down_sleep: Both clocks may be stopped after pending Tx complete + bus idle. m_can_clkstop_ack + CCCR.CSA = 1 signals 'ready for clock stop'.
low_power_modes_summary.bus_off: Forced shutdown of TX driver after TEC = 256; clocks remain running; CCCR.INIT set automatically; recovery requires 129 × Bus_Idle after CPU clears CCCR.INIT.

dual_clock_domain_concept.m_can_hclk: Host clock domain — drives Tx Handler / Rx Handler / Generic Slave Interface / Generic Master Interface / RAM Watchdog. May be a spread-spectrum (FM-PLL) clock for EMC.
dual_clock_domain_concept.m_can_cclk: CAN clock domain — drives CAN Core / Bit Stream Processor / Bit Timing Logic. Must be high-precision (no modulation) per the CAN FD bit-time tolerance requirements.
dual_clock_domain_concept.frequency_constraint: m_can_hclk frequency ≥ m_can_cclk frequency (spread-spectrum modulation depth must also be considered).
dual_clock_domain_concept.sync_block: Synchronizes signals + reset across the two domains.

fields.interrupt_during_power_down: The two CPU interrupt lines (m_can_int0 + m_can_int1) reflect the IR + IE + ILS + ILE state. During clock-stop (clocks halted), no new IR flags are set; existing latched flags remain visible until host clears them (W1C). Wake-up causes re-evaluation.
fields.notes: The M_CAN's power model is intentionally simple: one register-control bit (CCCR.CSR) + one pin (m_can_clkstop_req) gate the clock-stop request; the only protocol-level power feature is the clock-stop / wake-up sequence. Power-domain partitioning, retention strategy, and isolation cells are deferred to SoC + transceiver IP. The external transceiver typically supports its own low-power modes (sleep / standby) that wake on bus activity, asserting m_can_clkstop_req's deassertion via SoC power management logic.
